candidates: In Vitest test files, always place `vi.mock(...)` calls at the top of the file (outside any `describe` or `test` blocks) so Vitest's automatic hoisting works correctly. Use `vi.mock('module-name', { spy: true })` at the top level and configure mock return values or implementations inside `beforeEach` blocks rather than inline inside individual test cases.

When implementing string-split heuristics for type parsing (e.g., splitting on `' | '` to parse union types), add an inline comment documenting known edge cases that the heuristic cannot handle—such as nested unions inside generics (`Map<string, A | B>`) or function types with `=>` containing `|`—and note the recommended future improvement (e.g., parsing with the TypeScript AST or a proper tokenizer).

Avoid re-instantiating the `react-docgen-typescript` parser (via `withCompilerOptions`) on every call to the extraction function, since each call spins up a fresh TypeScript compiler Program. Cache the parser instance at module scope or via a closure so that repeated calls across components in the same Storybook session reuse the same Program.

When iterating over react-docgen `PropDescriptor` entries to extract type information, do not check only `tsType`. The `PropDescriptor` interface also has a `type` field used for JavaScript/PropTypes components; always fall back to `propInfo.type` when `propInfo.tsType` is absent so that non-TypeScript components are not silently dropped.

When selecting a component from react-docgen-typescript results by name, never use `filePath.includes(componentExportName)` substring matching—it produces false positives when one component name is a substring of another (e.g., 'Button' would match 'IconButton'). Prefer exact equality on `displayName` (and, where available, `actualName` or `exportName`). If file-path matching is genuinely required, use `path.basename(d.filePath, path.extname(d.filePath)) === componentExportName` for a strict comparison.

In `internal_getArgTypesData` (and similar preset functions that merge configuration from multiple sources), explicitly passed options (`reactDocgen`, `reactDocgenTypescriptOptions`) must take priority over values derived from `presets.apply(...)`. Always merge the two sources with the caller's explicit values winning, so that call sites that operate without a full presets chain (e.g., the vitest plugin) can still override docgen behavior rather than having their options silently ignored.
